stem:
Meena has read the chapter on magnets in her science book and can repeat every definition. At home in Jaipur, her grandmother asks her, "Have you really learnt the science?"

Which statement best shows that learning science goes beyond reading the book?

options.text: Meena has learnt the science because she can name all the magnetic materials from the book
Meena should watch her brother do the magnet activity so she can describe it in the test
Meena should test which spoons, pins and coins in the kitchen stick to a magnet and record what she observes
Meena should read the chapter once more until she memorises it fully

tables: {"headers":["Meena's plan","What it shows","Does it go beyond the book?"],"rows":[["naming magnetic materials from memory","recall of book content","no"],["watching someone else's activity","second-hand description","no"],["testing kitchen objects with a magnet and recording observations","observing and experimenting herself","yes"],["re-reading the chapter to memorise it","repetition of book content","no"]],"row_labels":["A","B","C","D"],"caption":"","is_option_table":true}

teacher.key_rationale: The chapter's claim is that science learning extends beyond reading into observing, doing activities and experimenting. Only option C has Meena herself experimenting and recording observations; A and D are pure book recall (condition-dropping traps), and B substitutes passive watching for doing.
